decisions.name: Jelena Vuckovic
decisions.summary: Research is nanophotonics and quantum/nonlinear optics; chip-scale photonic platforms are aimed in part at classical/quantum information processing, but the work is photonics physics (borderline: quantum-hardware and photonic inverse-design threads).

evidence.quote: Jelena Vuckovic’s research interests are broadly in the areas of nanophotonics, quantum and nonlinear optics. Her lab develops semiconductor-based photonic chip-scale systems with goals to probe new regimes of light-matter interaction, as well as to enable platforms for future classical and quantum information processing technologies.

decisions.name: Eric Pop
decisions.summary: Research is semiconductor nanoelectronics, 2D materials, thermal transport and data-storage devices: device/materials physics (borderline: memory devices; unlike H.-S. Philip Wong his statement does not frame the work as computing systems).

evidence.quote: His research interests include semiconductors, nanoelectronics, data storage, and energy.

decisions.name: Simon S. Wong
decisions.summary: Same person as "S. Simon Wong" and as census-additions/pis.json row "S Simon Wong": the 2016 EE listing names him "Simon S. Wong" and the 2019-2022 listings "S. decisions.computing_area: IC interconnects / RF and mixed-signal circuits

decisions.name: David A. B. Miller
decisions.summary: Optics and quantum-well optoelectronics, including optical interconnects for computing; the contribution is optical physics/devices, so computing is incidental (borderline). Now emeritus.

evidence.quote: David Miller’s research interests include the use of optics in switching, interconnection, communications, computing, and sensing systems, physics and applications of quantum well optics and optoelectronics, and fundamental features and limits for optics and nanophotonics in communications and information processing.

decisions.name: Shan X. Wang
decisions.summary: Magnetic nanotechnology, biosensors and spintronic storage devices: materials/device physics, not computing (borderline: MRAM/storage devices). Primary appointment MSE, jointly EE.

evidence.quote: He directs the Center for Magnetic Nanotechnology and is a leading expert in biosensors, information storage and spintronics.

decisions.name: Srabanti Chowdhury
decisions.summary: Wide-bandgap materials and devices for power and RF electronics: device physics, not computing.

evidence.quote: Wide bandap materials & devices for RF, Power and energy efficient electronics

decisions.name: Olav Solgaard
decisions.summary: Nanophotonics, micro-optics and MEMS: photonics/MEMS, not computing.

evidence.quote: The Solgaard group focus on design and fabrication of nano-photonics and micro-optical systems. We combine photonic crystals, optical meta-materials, silicon photonics, and MEMS, to create efficient and reliable systems for communication, sensing, imaging, and optical manipulation.

decisions.name: H. Tom Soh
decisions.summary: Analytical biotechnology (screening, directed evolution, biosensors): biology/bioengineering, not computing.

evidence.quote: His current research interests are in analytical biotechnology, especially in high-throughput screening, directed evolution, and integrated biosensors.

decisions.name: James S. Harris
decisions.summary: Compound-semiconductor materials growth and optoelectronic devices: materials/device physics, not computing.

evidence.quote: Harris utilizes molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) of III-V compound semiconductor materials to investigate new materials for electronic and optoelectronic devices.

decisions.name: Krishna Shenoy
decisions.summary: Neuroscience and neuroengineering of motor control and intracortical brain-machine interfaces; physiology/neuroengineering with computation as a tool, not computing (borderline: BCI decoding). Died 2023.

evidence.quote: We conduct neuroscience, neuroengineering and translational research to better understand how the brain controls movement, and to design medical systems to assist people with paralysis (see Fig. 1). These medical systems are referred to as brain-machine interfaces (BMIs), brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) and intra-cortical neural prostheses.

decisions.name: Piero A. Pianetta
decisions.summary: Synchrotron-based study of semiconductor interfaces: materials physics, not computing.

evidence.quote: Pianetta's research is directed towards understanding how the atomic and electronic structure of semiconductor interfaces impacts device technology pertaining to advanced semiconductors and photocathodes.

decisions.name: Krishna Saraswat
decisions.summary: Materials, structures and process technology of semiconductor devices and interconnects: device physics, not computing (borderline: memory/3D-IC device work).

evidence.quote: New and innovative materials, structures, and process technology of semiconductor devices, interconnects for nanoelectronics and solar cells.

decisions.name: Butrus Khuri-Yakub
decisions.summary: Ultrasound transducers, medical ultrasound and sensors: device/biomedical, not computing.

evidence.quote: His current research interests include medical ultrasound imaging and therapy, ultrasound neuro-stimulation, chemical/biological sensors, gas flow and energy flow sensing, micromachined ultrasonic transducers, and ultrasonic fl

decisions.name: Lambertus Hesselink
decisions.summary: Mainly nanophotonics, optical data storage and nonlinear optics (OpenAlex topics are optics-dominated); the image-processing/graphics and Internet-technology strands are minor, so not computing (borderline).

evidence.quote: Hesselink's research encompasses nano-photonics, ultra high density optical data storage, nonlinear optics, optical super-resolution, materials science, three-dimensional image processing and graphics, and Internet technologies.

decisions.name: James D. Plummer
decisions.summary: Silicon IC process/device technology (director of the IC Laboratory) and long-time dean of engineering: device physics/process technology, not computing.

evidence.quote: He joined the Stanford faculty in 1978 as an associate professor. He became professor of electrical engineering in 1983. His career at Stanford has included serving as director of the IC Laboratory, senior associate dean in the School of Engineering, and chair of the Electrical Engineering Department. He was the Frederick Emmons Terman Dean of the School of Engineering from 1999 until 2014.

decisions.name: Roger T. Howe
decisions.summary: MEMS/NEMS sensors and actuators: MEMS, not computing.

evidence.quote: Design and fabrication of sensors and actuators using micro and nanotechnologies, with applications to information processing and energy conversion.

decisions.name: Dwight G. Nishimura
decisions.summary: MRI acquisition (pulse-sequence) methods for cardiovascular imaging: medical imaging physics, not computing (borderline: reconstruction/processing is part of MRI methods).

evidence.quote: Nishimura develops new acquisition and processing techniques for improved medical imaging.

decisions.name: John T. Gill III
decisions.summary: Computing area (computational complexity, information theory, coding). No PI basis in 2016-2026: none of 18 archived Stanford Profiles captures 2015-2026 lists a Doctoral Dissertation Advisor (AC) or Postdoctoral Faculty Sponsor role; his 2016 profile shows teaching only, and he is now emeritus.

evidence.quote: John T. Gill III Associate Professor
Gill's research interests are in the areas of computational complexity theory and information theory, including probabilistic computation, lossless data compression, and error correcting codes.
Academic Appointments Emeritus Faculty, Acad Council, Electrical Engineering

decisions.name: Robert Dutton
decisions.summary: Technology CAD: numerical process/device simulation and parameter extraction for silicon technology. The object is semiconductor devices and the simulators serve device engineering, so computing is a method in service of device physics (borderline: TCAD is EDA-adjacent). He was still a PI in-window: Doctoral Dissertation Advisor (AC) of Timothy Anderson on 2019-2020 captures.

evidence.quote: Dutton's group develops and applies computer aids to process modeling and device analysis. His circuit design activities emphasize layout-related issues of parameter extraction and electrical behavior for devices that affect system performance. Activities include primarily silicon technology modeling both for digital and analog circuits, including OE/RF applications.

decisions.name: James F. Gibbons
decisions.summary: Semiconductor process physics (ion implantation, thin films); also emeritus/research only by 2016. Not computing.

evidence.quote: A pioneer in the use of ion implantation and rapid thermal process techniques for solid-state physics, Gibbons also conducts research into semiconductor device analysis, fabrication, and process physics.
